original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Prove that every rational decomposition I+2P = R+S+T into nonzero symmetric rank-one matrices is first-order character-excluded, and therefore the seven-call profile (a,b,p,q,r,s,t)=(1,1,0,2,1,1,1) admits no word.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian native alphabet. This package stays in the abelian symmetric 2-by-2 model and answers one three-frame census profile left open by the (2,0,1,1) exclusion.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the signed-frame escape. The profile still needs eight paid calls, so there is no local call-count saving and no selected-frontier change.
stop_rule: Stop after the character proof for the single printed profile (1,1,0,2)/(1,1,1), or after one explicit rational solution of that profile whose parity image contains (1,1). Do not survey the other printed profiles and do not take four or more added frames.
evidence: Elementary character proof for every rational rank-one solution of R+S+T=I+2P: the parity image in F2^2 avoids (1,1), so an AB or PQ form extends, and that form detects two calls and four targets. The scale bracket, axis numerator, axis rearrangement, and Cramer determinant are expanded polynomial identities. Lemma 4 exhausts 32 residue classes and Lemma 5 exhausts the three primitive classes modulo 2. Finite fixtures are in verify.py. The inherited first-order call inequality is not reproved.

open_questions.question: Which of the other seventeen three-frame count profiles printed in discussion comment 19377345 survive the same AB/PQ test?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only (1,1,1,1), (0,2,1,1), (2,0,1,1), and (1,1,0,2), each with added multiplicities (1,1,1), are character-excluded. A surviving profile would be the next place a seven-call word could exist.
open_questions.first_step: Read one tuple that comment 19377345 already prints, other than those four, write that tuple's own determinant residual, and test one rational rank-one solution with the bilinear form of that residual. The sign-flipped tuple (1,1,2,0)/(1,1,1) has residual [[2,-1],[-1,2]] and is not settled here.
open_questions.blocked_by: No uniform reduction among the remaining profiles is supplied, and the bilinear form 2 x1 y1 - x1 y2 - x2 y1 + 2 x2 y2 does not transfer off [[2,1],[1,2]].
